CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up of chronic medical problems

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male presenting for follow-up of depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension. Patient reports it has been a challenging year and a half. He experienced significant anxiety and stress related to holiday preparations, particularly Thanksgiving. He did attend Thanksgiving after approximately two years and found it rewarding to see family, though it was stressful and required substantial work. He is planning a vacation to somewhere warm in the new year.

Regarding depression: Patient continues to decline pharmacological therapy and is using non-pharmacological coping strategies. Over the summer, he initiated a routine of long walks outside each morning and enjoyed yard work on weekends, which he found beneficial for mood and provided physical activity and sun exposure. With seasonal changes and cold weather, he has been unable to maintain this routine and is seeking alternative strategies. He denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

Regarding diabetes: Patient reports managing reasonably well, doing okay through Halloween but not strictly adhering to diet during Thanksgiving week. He is currently monitoring intake more carefully.

Regarding hypertension: Patient purchased a home blood pressure cuff as recommended and reports readings have been moderate and normal with nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, blood in stool, or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Depression
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
- Metformin
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys outdoor activities including walking and gardening. Maintains contact with family and plans social activities.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well-controlled
Neck: No carotid bruits
Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at left base (previously noted)
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in lower extremities

RESULTS
EKG: No concerning findings
Hemoglobin A1C: 8% (elevated, goal <6%)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. Patient declines pharmacological intervention at this time.

2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8%. Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1C in next couple months. Order lipid panel.

3. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order echocardiogram to re-evaluate known systolic ejection murmur.
